item.title: Israeli military launches criminal probes into killings of 5-year-old and paramedics
item.description: Israel's military on Wednesday announced its first criminal investigations into troop conduct in Gaza, focusing on the killings of 5-year-old Hind Rajab and her family and of 15 Palestinian paramedics.
item.content:encoded:
Israel's military on Wednesday announced its first criminal investigations into troop conduct in Gaza, focusing on the killings of 5-year-old Hind Rajab and her family and of 15 Palestinian paramedics.

(Image credit: Jehad Alshrafi)

item.title: California passes toughest wildfire rules in the U.S. for home landscaping
item.description: California has adopted the toughest new rules in the country that require homeowners to manage the plants around their houses. Fire experts say it helps protect houses from burning, but public pushback has been strong.
item.content:encoded:
California has adopted the toughest new rules in the country that require homeowners to manage the plants around their houses. Fire experts say it helps protect houses from burning, but public pushback has been strong.

(Image credit: Mario Tama/Getty Images)

item.title: Experts raise alarms over Census Bureau report Trump is touting on noncitizen voting
item.description: A Trump-aligned think tank has ties to a highly unusual Census Bureau report that the president is using to renew false claims of widespread voting by non-U.S. citizens in 2020, NPR has learned.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The U.S. debt tops a record-shattering $40 trillion. Yes, with a T
item.description: The federal debt reached $40 trillion as the government adds red ink at a rapid rate. That's leading nervous investors to demand higher interest rates — pushing up borrowing costs for everyone else.

item.description: Dr. David Morens, a former aide to Dr. Anthony Fauci, has pleaded guilty to violating federal law by trying to conceal emails about the origins of the COVID-1 pandemic.

item.title: A real-world study of Oregon's nonmedical psilocybin program shows promise
item.description: Oregon was the first state to establish a legalized and regulated psilocybin industry. Since then, thousands have tried magic mushrooms. Here is the latest data from the state's real-life experiment.
